        {
          "@type": "Question",
          "name": "Who does the injections at Lumen Aesthetics?",
          "acceptedAnswer": {
            "@type": "Answer",
            "text": "Dr. Priya Nair, MD, Nadia R., NP, or Jess T., RN, per 118 reviews and the three licenses on the California boards. Not aestheticians."
          }
        },
        {
          "@type": "Question",
          "name": "How much is Botox at Lumen Aesthetics in Irvine?",
          "acceptedAnswer": {
            "@type": "Answer",
            "text": "$12 per unit, per the website in August 2026. Lumen has not confirmed current pricing."
          }
        },
        {
          "@type": "Question",
          "name": "Is the first consultation free?",
          "acceptedAnswer": {
            "@type": "Answer",
            "text": "Not published. One visitor reports paying $75 in March 2026, credited toward treatment booked the same day."
          }
        },
        {
          "@type": "Question",
          "name": "Where do you park for Lumen Aesthetics?",
          "acceptedAnswer": {
            "@type": "Answer",
            "text": "Structure B at the Irvine Spectrum, validated for two hours. Level 3 after 5 PM, per 14 visitors."
          }
        },
        {
          "@type": "Question",
          "name": "Is Lumen Aesthetics or Coastline MedSpa better?",
          "acceptedAnswer": {
            "@type": "Answer",
            "text": "Both are rated about the same. Visitors who went to both say Lumen for lips and filler, Coastline for lasers. Coastline replies to messages faster."
          }
        },
        {
          "@type": "Question",
          "name": "When is Lumen Aesthetics least busy?",
          "acceptedAnswer": {
            "@type": "Answer",
            "text": "Tuesday or Wednesday before 11 AM, per 12 weeks of foot-traffic data. Busiest Wednesday and Thursday from noon to 2 PM."
          }
        },

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      # Lumen Aesthetics, Irvine: a physician-owned med spa at the Irvine Spectrum (2026 guide)

Source: Local AI Registry, https://localairegistry.com/irvine-ca/med-spas/lumen-aesthetics. Free to reuse with a link back.

By Steve Lee, founder and CEO of Local AI Registry. Fact-checked against 69 sources. Updated 2026-09-25. Owner review: not yet.

Canonical: https://localairegistry.com/irvine-ca/med-spas/lumen-aesthetics

## In short

Lumen Aesthetics is a physician-owned med spa on the second floor of the Irvine Spectrum Center in Irvine, California, open since 2016. It is led by Dr. Priya Nair, MD, a board-certified dermatologist licensed by the Medical Board of California. It is best known for natural-looking dermal filler and Botox, holds a 4.9 average across 612 reviews on Google, Yelp and RealSelf, and charges $12 per unit of Botox and $780 per syringe of filler. It is open Tuesday to Saturday, 9 AM to 7 PM, and is quietest on Tuesday and Wednesday mornings.

Every fact on this page carries one of three marks: Confirmed (from their website, Google Business Profile, review sites, licensing boards, or measured by Local AI Registry), Visitor submitted (added by a person, with a date and how they know), or AI guess (what AI engines like ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude are saying, not confirmed by anyone). Every mark points to a reference at the end of this page.

4.9 average across 612 reviews: Google 412, Yelp 140, RealSelf 60. Lumen has replied to none of them. (Confirmed, read September 25, 2026.)

People come for filler that does not show and leave talking about Dr. Nair. The most repeated phrase across 612 reviews is some version of "you cannot tell I had anything done." ## How AI decides what to tell you about a med spa

When you ask ChatGPT, Gemini or Google for a med spa, the AI does not visit each business. It reads what is already written about it: the business website, its Google Business Profile, review sites like Yelp and RealSelf, news stories, licensing boards and directories like this one. Then it repeats what those sources agree on.

That is why AI gets small facts wrong. If Yelp says a place is open Mondays and the website says it is not, the AI has to pick one. The table above shows the answers that disagree with the record today.

The more sources agree, and the more specific they are, the more confidently AI recommends a business. A review that says "Nadia did half a syringe in my lips and it looks natural" is far more useful to an AI than one that says "great place."


## How to choose a med spa in California, with or without AI

A few checks take ten minutes and matter more than any rating. This is general information, not medical advice.

- Look up every injector. Doctors are on the Medical Board of California site; nurses and nurse practitioners are on the California Board of Registered Nursing site. Both are free.
- Ask who does the injections. In California, aestheticians cannot inject Botox or filler.
- Ask for the price per unit of Botox and per syringe of filler, not per area.
- Read reviews that name a provider and a treatment. Vague praise is easy to fake.
- Check that the hours and phone number match on Google, Yelp and the website. Mismatches are how people end up at a locked door.
- Ask whether they dissolve filler and when they would tell you not to add more.


## How to read the marks on this page

- Confirmed (solid circle): from a known source. The business website, its Google Business Profile, review sites like Yelp, Healthgrades and RealSelf, a licensing board, or measured by Local AI Registry.
- Visitor submitted (hollow circle): added or corrected by a person, with the date and how they know, like a phone call or a visit.
- AI guess (hollow triangle): what AI engines are saying right now. Nobody has confirmed it.

## Frequently asked questions


### Who does the injections at Lumen Aesthetics?

Dr. Priya Nair, MD, Nadia R., NP, or Jess T., RN, per 118 reviews and the three licenses on the California boards. Not aestheticians.


### How much is Botox at Lumen Aesthetics in Irvine?

$12 per unit, per the website in August 2026. Lumen has not confirmed current pricing.


### Is the first consultation free?

Not published. One visitor reports paying $75 in March 2026, credited toward treatment booked the same day.


### Where do you park for Lumen Aesthetics?

Structure B at the Irvine Spectrum, validated for two hours. Level 3 after 5 PM, per 14 visitors.


### Is Lumen Aesthetics or Coastline MedSpa better?

Both are rated about the same. Visitors who went to both say Lumen for lips and filler, Coastline for lasers. Coastline replies to messages faster.


### When is Lumen Aesthetics least busy?

Tuesday or Wednesday before 11 AM, per 12 weeks of foot-traffic data. Busiest Wednesday and Thursday from noon to 2 PM.


### Does Lumen Aesthetics offer Morpheus8 Body?

Yes. Consultations open October 1, 2026, per the practice's Instagram. Pricing was quoted by phone at $1,400 for arms.


### Is there a wait list for Morpheus8 Body?

### Lumen vs Coastline, which one?

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      For developers: what makes this page machine-readable
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • One source of truth. The page, the HTML, the JSON-LD and the markdown copy are generated from the same record, so they cannot disagree.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • 
    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Every entity has a stable @id and a sameAs link to a public reference: Wikipedia, a licensing board, or the entity's own site.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • 
    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • People are linked to their credentials, and credentials to the board that issued them (recognizedBy).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • 
    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Answers come first. The page opens with a one-paragraph summary and a key facts table, marked speakable.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • 
    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Wrong AI answers are published as ClaimReview, so engines can see the correction and its source.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • 
    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • The FAQ holds both our questions and real visitor questions, each with its answer.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • 
    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • robots.txt names every major AI crawler and allows it. The sitemap updates daily with lastmod.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • 
    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • A markdown copy sits at the same address with .md, linked from the HTTP headers, the head and llms.txt.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • 
    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • No text is hidden from people that crawlers can see. What machines read is what you read.
